title: Optimized protocol to isolate primary mouse peritoneal macrophage metabolites
protocol: Prepare a 10 mL syringe with 5 mL PM isolation media (Store at 4°C for up to 2 weeks) and attach a 27 g needle.
Keep the prepared syringe on ice.
Euthanize the mouse following an approved IACUC euthanasia protocol.
Place the euthanized mouse face-up on a sterile surface, pin down its limbs, and spray the abdomen with 70% EtOH.
Cut the skin overlying the peritoneum carefully without compromising the peritoneal cavity.
Expose the inner skin lining the peritoneal cavity gently using forceps and scissors.
Inject peritoneal cavity with 5 mL of PM isolation media.
Massage the abdominal walls for 10-25 seconds to dislodge attached peritoneal cells into the PM isolation media.
Use forceps to gently grasp and lift the peritoneum to create a tented space.
Insert needle filled with lavage fluid into the tented area.
Inject peritoneal lavage fluid.
Draw back up the PM isolation media using a new 10 mL syringe equipped with a 25 g needle.
Collect the peritoneal lavage in a 50 mL conical tube on ice.
Add PM isolation media to the 50 mL conical tube containing the peritoneal lavage up to the 30 mL mark.
Pellet peritoneal cells and perform RBC lysis.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 10 min to pellet cells.
Aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL RBC lysis buffer and pipette gently up and down until solution is homogenous.
Add additional 4 mL RBC lysis buffer and incubate for 5 min on ice.
Add PBS to a volume of 40 mL to quench the lysis immediately after the 5 min incubation period.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 10 min to pellet cells.
Aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend pelleted cells in 1 mL Complete RPMI media.
Split cells evenly into three groups: unstimulated PMs, LPS treatment group, and protein concentration measurement group.
Plate experimental groups (unstimulated and LPS treated) into one 24-well plate.
Plate the normalization well onto a new 24-well plate.
Incubate cells in a standard cell culture incubator for 2 hours.
Maintain incubator conditions at 37°C, CO2 concentration of ∼5%, and pH ∼7.3–7.5.
Prepare 13C-Glucose RPMI media and store it at 4°C for up to 2 weeks.
Bring the prepared 13C-Glucose RPMI media to 37°C in a water bath.
Prepare one tube with 13C-Glucose RPMI media.
Prepare another tube with LPS (200 ng/mL) in 13C-Glucose RPMI media.
Aspirate the media after 2 hours.
Wash remaining cells gently with 0.5 mL of PBS.
Add 0.5 mL of 13C-Glucose RPMI media or LPS + 13C-Glucose RPMI media.
Incubate at 37°C, CO2 concentration ∼5%, and pH ∼7.3–7.5 for 4 hours.
Measure the total protein concentration in the normalization well using Pierce BCA Kit.
Calculate the total protein per well.
Determine the amount of metabolite isolation reagent needed (80% acetonitrile LC-MS grade and 20% H2O HPLC grade).
Dilute samples to a final concentration of 0.5–1 μg/μL in metabolite isolation reagent.
Prepare the Metabolite isolation reagent and store it at -20°C for at least 2 hours before use.
Label two sets of 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes and prechill them on ice.
After the 4-hour labeling incubation, aspirate the labeling media from the wells.
Wash each well with 0.5 mL of PBS and aspirate the PBS.
Place the plates on ice and add Metabolite isolation reagent based on normalization well concentration to each sample.
Using a pipette tip, pipette up and down in each well to homogenize the solution without generating bubbles.
Scrape the bottom of the well with the pipette tip to dislodge any cells.
Transfer the solution to prechilled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Vortex each sample once for 15 seconds.
Freeze the lysates at -80°C for 1 hour.
Pause and freeze samples at -80°C for 16–24 h if necessary.
Thaw lysates on ice after 1 hour or the next day, then vortex for 15 seconds.
Centrifuge lysates at 20,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer supernatant to new microcentrifuge tubes and place on ice.
Store samples in -80°C for up to a month or freeze in liquid nitrogen for up to 6 months if not proceeding immediately to MS analysis.
